Aldershot event to revisit Alf Burtoo's 1983 UFO story

Aldershot’s North Town Community Centre will revisit the famous 1983 UFO story of Alf Burtoo. (Image: supplied)

This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.

A UFO encounter with a very British twist is taking centre stage in a Hampshire community.

Aldershot’s North Town Community Centre will host a gathering at noon on Saturday, November 21, to revisit the famous 1983 UFO story of Alf Burtoo, the 77-year-old fisherman who claimed to have been invited onto an alien craft before being told he was "too old and too infirm" to stay.

Cllr Keith Dibble said: "I knew Alf well, he was a friend.

"To his dying day he believed this happened.

"Come along on Saturday and make up your own mind."

The event promises tea, coffee, cake and conversation about Mr Burtoo’s case and other unexplained phenomena.

Attendees are encouraged to share their own theories and stories.

A spokesperson said: "Shortly after one in the morning on 12 August 1983, a 77-year-old angler put down his tea on a Hampshire canal bank to watch a silent light settle onto the towpath, and his evening took a turn.

"Come and hear the case as it was recorded, then tell us what you make of it.

"This is the day to share."
